headline: Saturday took the war to Riyadh's airport — and Trump flipped on joining the strikes. The haven bid has fresh fuel for Sunday's reopen.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: Saturday brought the war to Riyadh's airport — and Trump flipped from 'no strikes before the midterms' to 'we may' join the Saudi campaign. The hawkish hold survives the weekend untouched.
chapters.fx: What to watch: the Sunday 5pm ET FX reopen is the first price test of Saturday's escalation — the gap is likelier risk-off than risk-on. Monday is Columbus Day: US bond markets are closed, so liquidity runs thin while FX spot trades normally. Then the real week begins: RBA minutes and the French budget debate Tuesday, China CPI and the main event — US CPI Wednesday at 7:30am CT. On the diplomacy side: whether Trump picks up Putin's broker channel, and Iran's reply on the US counterproposal due within days. Off the beaten path: India's RBI opened a dollar window for oil importers Saturday as the rupee tests its record low — worth watching for Asia-FX transmission at the reopen, not a dollar story yet.
chapters.meaning: What changed: Saturday delivered three genuine developments — two on the escalation side, one on the diplomacy side. First, missiles hit Terminals 3 and 4 of Riyadh's King Khalid Airport — the third attack on the airport this week — wounding dozens, closing the airport, and forcing flights to divert or cancel. Diplomatic sources blame the Houthis, who claimed this week's earlier attacks (including Thursday's, which killed three Saudis); there is no immediate claim for Saturday's, and the kingdom's early-warning system never sounded. Second, Trump flipped twice: at a Friday rally he re-threatened Iran ('either they give us everything, or they don't exist any longer'), and Saturday he told reporters the US 'may' join Saudi strikes on the Houthis — a clean reversal of his own Thursday pledge of no strikes before the Nov 3 midterms. The Saudi coalition says it destroyed 136 Houthi targets in retaliation — the coalition's own claim, not independently verified. Third, the diplomacy track: the Kremlin said Saturday that Putin relayed Iran's position on a possible resolution of the US–Iran conflict to Trump in a Friday call — done 'in coordination with' Iran's president after Putin met him twice in Turkmenistan on Thursday, offering Russia as a broker. Terms undisclosed, Trump's response undisclosed, and the White House hasn't confirmed the call — treat it as a channel opening, not a breakthrough. Thread: the hawkish hold is in week four — Dec ~82% priced, October ~18% (CME, via Reuters), claims held 197k for a fourth straight week. Friday evening added the two curveballs (the widened strike campaign and the diesel deal). What it means: confirms the thesis. Saturday changed nothing about the Fed's path — there were no data prints, and a war story is not a rate story — but it deepened the escalation side. The dollar enters Sunday with the haven bid re-armed rather than repriced — and now with a genuine two-way setup: Saturday stacked escalation headlines (Riyadh, Trump's flip) against a diplomacy headline (Putin's broker offer). The market's question at the reopen is which side of the ledger the tape weights.
numbers: DXY ~102.0–102.2 (−0.3% Fri; +0.6% w/w, 7th straight weekly gain)
Dec hike ~82% priced; Oct ~18% (CME, via Reuters)
Sunday 5pm ET: first price test of Saturday's escalation

scenarios.base: Reopen gaps modestly risk-off, the haven bid firms, USD holds its bid into CPI week.
scenarios.bear: The reopen shrugs or leans into Putin's broker channel; the haven bid leaks and DXY slips back toward 101.
scenarios.bull: Fresh weekend escalation plus gap-higher oil — December gets fully priced and DXY extends to fresh highs.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: Nothing changed Saturday — EUR/USD rests near 1.12, and the fiscal dossier waits for Tuesday's budget debate.
chapters.fx: What to watch: the French budget plenary Tuesday Oct 13 (votes run late Nov–mid Dec), German ZEW the same morning, and the Aa3 rating review this month. The 1.1161 line still holds: a break risks 1.1065; a hold plus calm spreads opens a relief bounce toward 1.13.
chapters.meaning: What changed: nothing — Saturday brought no euro news, and EUR/USD carries Friday's ~1.12 close into the weekend. Thread: the bleeding paused but didn't reverse — four weeks of French fiscal stress layered onto ECB-policy drag, the OAT–Bund spread at ~140–146bp off the 150bp+ wides, debt/GDP at 119.3% heading to 121.7% in 2027, the 2026 growth forecast cut to 0.5%. What it means: confirms — the fiscal risk premium stays priced in, and the dollar side of the pair (see the USD chapter) does the rest. This is a waiting chapter, and it's worth saying so plainly: Tuesday is the next event.

scenarios.base: EUR/USD pinned near 1.12 into Tuesday's budget debate; fiscal premium holds.
scenarios.bear: 1.1161 breaks or the budget debate turns ugly — next downside magnet 1.1065.
scenarios.bull: Smooth debate + calm spreads — relief toward 1.13.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: Sterling spent Saturday doing nothing — $1.324 and a 16-month high vs the euro, the floor still holding.
chapters.fx: What to watch: UK Sep CPI (the number that decides whether the BoE's hike case survives), BRC retail sales, and Chancellor Healey's first Budget Oct 28. The 1.3180 floor — five holds in seven sessions — is the line.
chapters.meaning: What changed: nothing Saturday — GBP/USD carries Friday's ~$1.324 into the weekend, sterling holding its 16-month high against the euro at 84.74p. Thread: the BoE's 6–3 hawkish hold stands, November's hike ~85% priced, the 30-year gilt still above 6%. Friday confirmed the floor-traders' logic — a market this short doesn't have many new sellers left. What it means: confirms — sterling remains the relative winner of Europe's fiscal stress, bid vs the euro and floored by BoE hike pricing. The one-sided risk is unchanged: if the Oct 28 Budget spooks gilts, real-money selling joins the existing shorts.

scenarios.base: GBP consolidates the 1.32 area; hawkish-hold keeps a floor under it.
scenarios.bear: A Budget that spooks gilts — GBP gives back the euro-driven gains fast.
scenarios.bull: Hot UK CPI cements the November hike — GBP/USD pushes toward 1.34.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: Saturday re-armed the yen's haven catalyst — it goes into Sunday with a 62k-strong spec long crowd and fresh fuel.
chapters.fx: What to watch: the Sunday 5pm ET reopen — do the bids push USD/JPY through 157? Above, 159–160 resistance and any MoF/BoJ intervention rhetoric. US CPI Wednesday moves the 10Y first, then this pair.
chapters.meaning: What changed: no price move — FX was closed — but the catalyst pile grew. Saturday's Riyadh airport strikes and Trump's flip on joining the Saudi campaign are exactly the kind of news the reopen reprices first, and the yen is the cleanest G10 haven for it. Thread: USD/JPY closed Friday at 157.87 (−0.37%), and specs rebuilt yen longs to 62,325 contracts in the week to Oct 6 (CFTC, released Friday), up from 55,440 — the yen-long crowd is growing again. The US–Japan rate gap still owns the pair: a US 10-year near 5.25% against a BoJ at 1.25%, OIS pricing a December BoJ hike above 80%, the Oct 29–30 meeting live, and PM Takaichi's 'appropriate action' intervention language on the tape. What it means: confirms — the tension tightens. The yield gap caps any yen rally, but the yen now enters Sunday with both a crowd and a fresh catalyst. The dollar side of the pair (see the USD chapter) decides the gap; the Gulf decides the fear.
numbers: CFTC JPY net longs 62,325 (wk to Oct 6; up from 55,440)

scenarios.base: Rate gap dominates; USD/JPY consolidates below 159–160 while intervention talk caps the top.
scenarios.bear: The reopen shrugs at Saturday's news; the yield gap reasserts and 159–160 comes back into play.
scenarios.bull: Saturday's escalation gaps at the reopen — the yen rallies and USD/JPY breaks lower through 157.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: Saturday made the franc's job simple — it's a pure fear barometer, and fear just got more fuel for the reopen.
chapters.fx: What to watch: the Sunday 5pm ET reopen — does the haven bid extend or fade? Any fresh Iran/Saudi headline over the weekend.
chapters.meaning: What changed: no price move (closed), but the tape feeding the reopen changed: missiles on Riyadh's airport twice, Trump flipping on strikes. Thread: USD/CHF fell to 0.8302 (−0.17%) Friday as the haven bid returned, and the SNB is pinned at 0.00% (next decision Dec 10) — there is no domestic rate story at all, so this pair moves only on fear. What it means: confirms the break — CHF spent the week softening on de-escalation, Friday evening put the haven bid back, and Saturday gave it reason to stay. The Sunday reopen tells whether it's a one-day repricing or a new leg.

scenarios.base: CHF firms into the reopen on Saturday's escalation; USD/CHF drifts lower.
scenarios.bear: The reopen shrugs — the haven bid leaks out again.
scenarios.bull: Fresh Tehran move over the weekend — CHF extends as fear trades.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The cleanest risk proxy in G10 goes into Sunday with the weekend's escalation stacked against it.
chapters.fx: What to watch: the Sunday 5pm ET reopen first — risk proxies gap first on any headline, and Friday evening's pattern is the warning (best G10 at 4pm, weakest by the close). Then RBA minutes Tuesday Oct 13, Australia jobs Thursday Oct 15, China CPI Wednesday Oct 14.
chapters.meaning: What changed: no price move (closed), but the setup worsened. Friday evening taught the lesson: the Aussie sold first and asked later when the strikes widened. Saturday added Riyadh's airport and Trump's flip — so the reopen risk is skewed to a lower gap. Thread: AUD/USD closed Friday at ~0.6986 (−0.11%), the RBA sits hawkish on hold at 4.60%, China is back from Golden Week (Shanghai reopened Thursday with a −0.79% catch-up selloff, then firmed Friday with the Hang Seng up 1.5%), and the yuan sits ~6.694. What it means: confirms and sharpens the prior thesis — AUD is the cleanest expression of the risk mood in G10, in both directions. The RBA tailwind is real, but when the Gulf headlines hit, the proxy sells first.
numbers: RBA 4.60% on hold; minutes Tue Oct 13

scenarios.base: AUD trades the risk mood into the reopen — soft on escalation, firm on calm.
scenarios.bear: Saturday's escalation gaps at the reopen — AUD opens lower, 0.6930 back in play.
scenarios.bull: Reopen holds plus soft US CPI Wednesday — risk-on, AUD reclaims 0.70.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: Saturday's strikes thickened Brent's floor — but the 161bp rate gap still owns the loonie.
chapters.fx: What to watch: does crude gap higher at the Sunday reopen and give CAD a reprieve? Then Canada CPI Oct 21, then the BoC decision Oct 28.
chapters.meaning: What changed: no price move (closed), but Brent's $104.72 settle got a thicker floor Saturday — Riyadh's airport, Trump's flip, the coalition's retaliation claims all lean on the same geopolitical premium. Thread: the loonie holds 18-month lows (USD/CAD 1.4257) with the two forces in its tape fighting to a draw. The −68.3K jobs shock anchors the downside: Oct 28 BoC hike odds sit at ~25%, and the ~161bp US–Canada 2Y gap (widest since Feb 2025) is the weight on every rally. The hawkish-BoC thesis is broken — the market prices the BoC on hold at best, and a currency that was trading the oil premium is now trading the rate gap. What it means: confirms — terms of trade giveth, the rate gap taketh away. Saturday tilts the near-term balance back toward the oil side, but nothing changes the BoC math until Canada CPI Oct 21.

scenarios.base: CAD pinned — oil tailwind fights the rate gap; USD/CAD stays elevated.
scenarios.bear: Canada CPI soft Oct 21 — BoC leans dovish, USD/CAD extends toward 1.45.
scenarios.bull: Saturday's escalation gaps crude higher at the reopen — CAD gets an oil-driven reprieve.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: Still the quietest chapter — ~0.5613, waiting on the RBNZ's Oct 28 two-way bet.
chapters.fx: What to watch: the Sunday reopen with the rest of the risk bloc; the RBNZ decision Oct 28 (01:00 UTC) — pause vs hike is still a genuine two-way bet.
chapters.meaning: What changed: nothing Saturday — NZD/USD carries Friday's ~0.5613 into the weekend, drifting with the risk bloc. Thread: Westpac's call stands — pause Oct 28, 25bp hike in December instead (OCR 2.75%), two more in early 2027. What it means: the two-way-bet thesis holds unchanged. A currency waiting on its central bank and on the risk mood, with nothing this weekend to move it either way.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Saturday took the strike campaign to Riyadh's airport — the ~$14 Brent–WTI spread has fresh reason to stay wide into Sunday.
chapters.fx: What to watch: the spread itself — past $15 means Hormuz risk is back in force; toward $5 means the premium is truly unwinding. Sunday's reopen is the first price test of Saturday's escalation. On the diplomacy side: if Putin's broker channel gains traction, the premium softens — that's the path to a sub-$100 Brent and a collapsing spread. For CAD, WTI is the number that moves the terms of trade; for JPY/EUR importers, Brent.
chapters.meaning: What changed: Saturday widened the campaign to Saudi territory. Missiles hit Terminals 3 and 4 of Riyadh's King Khalid Airport — the third attack this week — wounding dozens and closing the airport, while Trump flipped from no-strikes-before-midterms to 'we may' join the Saudi campaign, and the coalition claims 136 Houthi targets destroyed in retaliation. Brent's $104.72 settle (+$0.44 on Friday, +2.4% on the week) goes into Sunday with a thicker floor. Thread: Friday evening re-priced the tape when an unclaimed projectile struck the Trafigura-chartered VLCC Gem No 2 off the UAE and the IRGC officially claimed the NV Sunshine hit, warning of 'punishment' across the region — the strikes moving beyond the strait. ING's read from Friday stands: the market is 'reluctant to price out the geopolitical premium' above $100. What it means: the number that matters isn't either price, it's the ~$14 gap between them — roughly triple-to-quadruple the normal spread. The premium is the geopolitical/shipping risk, living in Brent (the seaborne benchmark exposed to Hormuz), while WTI (~$90.6–90.9, landlocked in Oklahoma) barely feels it. One counterweight for the bear case: Kpler data via aggregators had Hormuz flows at 19.5–22.5M bpd Sep 27–29, back above pre-war levels — the physical disruption so far is in the risk, not the barrels. The Trump–Putin diesel deal (~4.8M tons, Treasury license through Apr 7, 2027) stays a sideshow for crude: ~6M barrels is ≈1.5 days of US demand (Pickering via CNN) — diesel fell 3%, crude barely moved. Side notes: Hurricane Isaias shut ~1.3 mbpd of Gulf output (62.9%), and China resumed refined-fuel exports post-Golden Week (3.7mt) — modest diesel relief.
numbers: Isaias: 62.9% of Gulf output shut (~1.3 mbpd)

scenarios.base: Brent drifts $100–106 into the reopen; the spread stays wide while strikes continue.
scenarios.bear: Hormuz reopening progress, flows holding, or Putin's broker channel gaining traction — Brent breaks under $100, spread collapses toward $5.
scenarios.bull: Fresh weekend escalation: Brent spikes toward $110+, spread blows past $15.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold goes into Sunday with both legs loaded — the anti-dollar and the war hedge.
chapters.fx: What to watch: a break back above $4,300 would signal the haven bid is broadening beyond dollar-weakness — historically a USD-negative, CHF/JPY-positive setup. Conversely, a hot CPI Wednesday that revives hike bets would likely knock gold back toward $4,000.
chapters.meaning: What changed: no price move (closed) — but Saturday's escalation re-arms the war-hedge leg for the reopen. Thread: gold jumped ~1–1.4% to ~$4,170–4,190 Friday on the full package — a softer dollar, easing yields, and the evening's escalation arriving together. It sits ~22% below January's $5,318 peak, after months bleeding lower as the Fed's hawkish hold kept real yields elevated and the dollar ripped to 18-month highs. What it means: Friday was the first day in a while gold worked as both trades at once — the anti-dollar and the war hedge. Saturday's news gives the haven leg fresh fuel into Sunday; CPI Wednesday decides the dollar leg.

scenarios.base: Gold consolidates $4,100–4,300 into Wednesday's CPI; direction comes from the print, not the metal.
scenarios.bear: Hot CPI revives the October hike; real yields jump and gold slides back toward $4,000.
scenarios.bull: CPI undershoots and hike bets collapse — gold breaks $4,300 and the anti-dollar trade broadens.
